subject: math
title: Multiplying and Dividing with Unit Fractions
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplying and Dividing with Unit Fractions Worksheets: 4 × 1/3, 3 ÷ 1/4 (Free, Answer Key, Ontario)
short_title: Multiplying and dividing with unit fractions
standard_text: Multiply and divide one-digit whole numbers by unit fractions, using appropriate tools and drawings
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing whole numbers by unit fractions: 4 × 1/3 with bar models, mixed-number answers, 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, choosing × or ÷, and word problems with pizza slices and laps. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Ontario curriculum.
key_big: 4 × 1/3 = 4 thirds = 4/3. 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many fourths are in 3: 3 × 4 = 12.
key_sub: Multiplying by a unit fraction gives a smaller answer, so keep the denominator and count the pieces. Dividing by a unit fraction gives a bigger answer, because every whole holds as many pieces as the denominator.
body_html:
The big idea

A unit fraction has 1 on top, like 13 or 18. × a unit fraction means “groups of that piece”. 4 × 13 is 4 thirds. ÷ a unit fraction asks “how many pieces fit?” 3 ÷ 14 asks how many fourths are in 3.

Whole number × unit fraction

Count the pieces. The whole number tells how many pieces. The denominator stays the same.

Example

5 × 16 = ?

5 pieces of 1 sixth make 5 sixths.

Answer: 56

Writing the answer as a mixed number

When the top number is bigger than the bottom number, make full wholes. Divide the top by the bottom.

Example

9 × 14 = ?

9 × 14 = 94. 9 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 1, so 2 wholes and 1 fourth.

Answer: 2 14

Whole number ÷ unit fraction

Each whole has as many pieces as the denominator. Multiply the whole number by the denominator.

Example

5 ÷ 13 = ?

Each whole has 3 thirds. 5 × 3 = 15 thirds.

Answer: 15

× or ÷?

The story says…UseExample
equal groups of a piece: “how much in all?”×3 days of 14 sandwich: 3 × 14 = 34
“how many pieces fit?”, “how many laps?”÷How many 14 km laps in 3 km? 3 ÷ 14 = 12

Check your answer: multiplying by a unit fraction gives a smaller answer. Dividing by a unit fraction gives a bigger answer.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 ÷ 14 = 34 (multiplying instead of dividing)Count the fourths: each whole has 4, so 3 wholes have 12. 3 ÷ 14 = 12.
4 × 13 = 412 (multiplying the denominator too)Only the number of pieces changes: 4 thirds = 43.
73 = 7 13 (writing the whole number in front)7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1, so 73 = 2 13.

faq.q: How do you multiply a whole number by a unit fraction in Grade 5?
faq.a: Multiply the whole number by the numerator 1 and keep the denominator. For example, 4 × 1/3 = 4/3, which is 1 1/3.

faq.q: How do you divide a whole number by a unit fraction?
faq.a: Ask how many pieces fit. Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4 = 12, because each whole has 4 fourths.
Dividing by 1/4 counts how many fourths are in 3. There are 4 fourths in every whole, so there are 12 fourths in 3.

faq.q: Is multiplying and dividing by unit fractions in the Grade 5 Ontario curriculum?
faq.a: Yes. Expectation B2.8 in the Grade 5 Number strand asks students to multiply and divide one-digit whole numbers by unit fractions, using tools and drawings.

sets.title: Whole number × unit fraction with bars

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 13 of each bar is shaded. What is 4 × 13?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4 bars with 1 third each. 4 × 13 means 4 groups of 13. That is 4 thirds, so the answer is 43. 4 ÷ 3 = 1 remainder 1, so it is 1 13.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 15 of each bar is shaded. What is 3 × 15?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 bars with 1 fifth each. 3 × 15 means 3 groups of 15. That is 3 fifths, so the answer is 35.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 12 of each bar is shaded. What is 5 × 12?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 5 bars with 1 half each. 5 × 12 means 5 groups of 12. That is 5 halves, so the answer is 52. 5 ÷ 2 = 2 remainder 1, so it is 2 12.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 13 of each bar is shaded. What is 2 × 13?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 2 bars with 1 third each. 2 × 13 means 2 groups of 13. That is 2 thirds, so the answer is 23.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 16 of each bar is shaded. What is 5 × 16?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 5 bars with 1 sixth each. 5 × 16 means 5 groups of 16. That is 5 sixths, so the answer is 56.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 14 of each bar is shaded. What is 7 × 14?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 7 bars with 1 fourth each. 7 × 14 means 7 groups of 14. That is 7 fourths, so the answer is 74. 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3, so it is 1 34.

items.q: Each jump is 14. Where do 3 jumps from 0 land? 3 × 14 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 3 jumps of 14. 3 × 14 means 3 groups of 14. That is 3 fourths, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Each jump is 13. Where do 5 jumps from 0 land? 5 × 13 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 5 jumps of 13. 5 × 13 means 5 groups of 13. That is 5 thirds, so the answer is 53. 5 ÷ 3 = 1 remainder 2, so it is 1 23.

items.q: Each jump is 15. Where do 2 jumps from 0 land? 2 × 15 = ?

items.q: Each jump is 12. Where do 7 jumps from 0 land? 7 × 12 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 7 jumps of 12. 7 × 12 means 7 groups of 12. That is 7 halves, so the answer is 72. 7 ÷ 2 = 3 remainder 1, so it is 3 12.

items.e: 2 × 17 means 2 groups of 17. That is 2 sevenths, so the answer is 27.

items.e: 18 × 3 is the same as 3 × 18. 3 × 18 means 3 groups of 18. That is 3 eighths, so the answer is 38.

items.e: 112 × 5 is the same as 5 × 112. 5 × 112 means 5 groups of 112. That is 5 twelfths, so the answer is 512.

Write the answer as a fraction.
items.e: 14 × 9 is the same as 9 × 14. 9 × 14 means 9 groups of 14. That is 9 fourths, so the answer is 94. 9 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 1, so it is 2 14.

items.q: 15 + 15 + 15 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 fifths, so the sum is 35. Do not add the denominators: the pieces are still fifths. This is the same as 3 × 15.

items.q: Which multiplication is the same as 16 + 16 + 16 + 16?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 16, so it is 4 × 16 = 46. Check the other choices: 6 × 14 = 64, 4 × 6 = 24, and 4 + 16 = 4 16.

items.q: ? × 18 = 58
items.e: 58 means 5 eighths. 5 groups of 18 make 5 eighths, so the missing number is 5. Check: 5 × 18 = 58.

items.q: Which is the same as 3 × 14?
items.e: 3 × 14 is 3 groups of 1 fourth, which is 3 fourths = 34.

items.q: The shaded parts show 7 × 13 = 73. Write it as a mixed number.
items.e: Count the full bars, then the extra pieces. 7 × 13 = 73. 3 thirds make 1 whole. 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1: 2 wholes and 1 third left over. So 73 = 2 13.

items.q: The shaded parts show 5 × 12 = 52. Write it as a mixed number.
items.e: Count the full bars, then the extra pieces. 5 × 12 = 52. 2 halves make 1 whole. 5 ÷ 2 = 2 remainder 1: 2 wholes and 1 half left over. So 52 = 2 12.

items.q: The shaded parts show 9 × 14 = 94. Write it as a mixed number.
items.e: Count the full bars, then the extra pieces. 9 × 14 = 94. 4 fourths make 1 whole. 9 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 1: 2 wholes and 1 fourth left over. So 94 = 2 14.

items.e: Count the full bars, then the extra pieces. 7 × 15 = 75. 5 fifths make 1 whole. 7 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 2: 1 whole and 2 fifths left over. So 75 = 1 25.

items.e: Count the full bars, then the extra pieces. 8 × 13 = 83. 3 thirds make 1 whole. 8 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 2: 2 wholes and 2 thirds left over. So 83 = 2 23.

items.q: 6 × 13 = ?
items.e: 6 × 13 means 6 groups of 13. That is 6 thirds, so the answer is 63. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so it is 2 wholes.

items.q: 8 × 14 = ?
items.e: 8 × 14 means 8 groups of 14. That is 8 fourths, so the answer is 84. 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so it is 2 wholes.

items.q: 9 × 13 = ?
items.e: 9 × 13 means 9 groups of 13. That is 9 thirds, so the answer is 93. 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so it is 3 wholes.

items.q: Between which two whole numbers is 7 × 12?
items.e: 7 × 12 = 72. 7 ÷ 2 = 3 remainder 1, so it is 3 12. That is between 3 and 4.

items.q: Which is greater: 7 × 14 or 2?
items.e: 7 × 14 = 74 = 1 34. 2 wholes would be 8 fourths, and 7 fourths is 1 fourth less. So 2 is greater.

items.q: Each whole is cut into fourths. How many fourths are in 3? 3 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: 3 ÷ 14 asks how many fourths are in 3. Each whole has 4 fourths, so 3 wholes have 3 × 4 = 12 fourths. Check: 12 × 14 = 124 = 3.

items.q: Each whole is cut into thirds. How many thirds are in 2? 2 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: 2 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds are in 2. Each whole has 3 thirds, so 2 wholes have 2 × 3 = 6 thirds. Check: 6 × 13 = 63 = 2.

items.q: Each whole is cut into halves. How many halves are in 4? 4 ÷ 12 = ?
items.e: 4 ÷ 12 asks how many halves are in 4. Each whole has 2 halves, so 4 wholes have 4 × 2 = 8 halves. Check: 8 × 12 = 82 = 4.

items.q: Each whole is cut into fifths. How many fifths are in 2? 2 ÷ 15 = ?
items.e: 2 ÷ 15 asks how many fifths are in 2. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 2 wholes have 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Check: 10 × 15 = 105 = 2.

items.q: Each whole is cut into thirds. How many thirds are in 3? 3 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: 3 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds are in 3. Each whole has 3 thirds, so 3 wholes have 3 × 3 = 9 thirds. Check: 9 × 13 = 93 = 3.

items.q: Each whole is cut into sixths. How many sixths are in 2? 2 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: 2 ÷ 16 asks how many sixths are in 2. Each whole has 6 sixths, so 2 wholes have 2 × 6 = 12 sixths. Check: 12 × 16 = 126 = 2.

items.q: Each jump is 14. How many jumps from 0 to 2? 2 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 4 in each whole. 2 ÷ 14 asks how many fourths are in 2. Each whole has 4 fourths, so 2 wholes have 2 × 4 = 8 fourths. Check: 8 × 14 = 84 = 2.

items.q: Each jump is 12. How many jumps from 0 to 3? 3 ÷ 12 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 2 in each whole. 3 ÷ 12 asks how many halves are in 3. Each whole has 2 halves, so 3 wholes have 3 × 2 = 6 halves. Check: 6 × 12 = 62 = 3.

items.q: Each jump is 15. How many jumps from 0 to 3? 3 ÷ 15 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 5 in each whole. 3 ÷ 15 asks how many fifths are in 3. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 3 wholes have 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Check: 15 × 15 = 155 = 3.

items.q: Each jump is 13. How many jumps from 0 to 4? 4 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Count the jumps: 3 in each whole. 4 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds are in 4. Each whole has 3 thirds, so 4 wholes have 4 × 3 = 12 thirds. Check: 12 × 13 = 123 = 4.

items.q: 5 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: 5 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds are in 5. Each whole has 3 thirds, so 5 wholes have 5 × 3 = 15 thirds. Check: 15 × 13 = 153 = 5.

items.q: 4 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: 4 ÷ 16 asks how many sixths are in 4. Each whole has 6 sixths, so 4 wholes have 4 × 6 = 24 sixths. Check: 24 × 16 = 246 = 4.

items.q: 7 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: 7 ÷ 14 asks how many fourths are in 7. Each whole has 4 fourths, so 7 wholes have 7 × 4 = 28 fourths. Check: 28 × 14 = 284 = 7.

items.q: 9 ÷ 15 = ?
items.e: 9 ÷ 15 asks how many fifths are in 9. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 9 wholes have 9 × 5 = 45 fifths. Check: 45 × 15 = 455 = 9.

items.q: 6 ÷ 18 = ?
items.e: 6 ÷ 18 asks how many eighths are in 6. Each whole has 8 eighths, so 6 wholes have 6 × 8 = 48 eighths. Check: 48 × 18 = 488 = 6.

items.q: 2 ÷ 112 = ?
items.e: 2 ÷ 112 asks how many twelfths are in 2. Each whole has 12 twelfths, so 2 wholes have 2 × 12 = 24 twelfths. Check: 24 × 112 = 2412 = 2.

items.q: Ethan says 3 ÷ 14 = 34. What mistake did he make?
c: He multiplied by 14 instead of dividing.
He counted the fourths in 1 whole only.
items.e: 3 × 14 = 34, so Ethan multiplied. 3 ÷ 14 asks how many fourths are in 3. Each whole has 4 fourths, so the answer is 3 × 4 = 12, which is more than 3.

items.q: Which is the same as 6 ÷ 13?
items.e: 6 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds are in 6. Each whole has 3 thirds, so it is 6 × 3 = 18. 6 × 13 and 6 ÷ 3 are both 2, and 3 ÷ 6 is 12.

items.q: ? ÷ 15 = 30
items.e: Each whole has 5 fifths. How many wholes make 30 fifths? 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Check: 6 ÷ 15 = 6 × 5 = 30.
24 ÷ 8 = 3, so each whole holds 3 equal pieces. The pieces are thirds: 8 ÷ 13 = 8 × 3 = 24. The missing number is 13.

items.q: Olivia eats 14 of a sandwich each day for 3 days. How much sandwich does she eat in all? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each day is one group of 14. There are 3 equal groups of 14, so multiply: 3 × 14 = 34.

items.q: A bag holds 3 cups of flour. A scoop holds 14 cup. How many scoops of flour are in the bag? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 14 cup scoops make 3 cups. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 3 ÷ 14 = 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: Each of 5 friends drinks 13 L of juice. How much juice do they drink altogether? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each friend is one group of 13 L. There are 5 equal groups of 13, so multiply: 5 × 13 = 1 23.

items.q: Emma has a 2 m board. She cuts it into pieces that are each 13 m long. How many pieces does she get? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 13 m pieces fit in 2 m. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 2 ÷ 13 = 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: A muffin recipe uses 12 cup of oats for each batch. How many cups of oats do 7 batches need? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each batch is one group of 12 cup. There are 7 equal groups of 12, so multiply: 7 × 12 = 3 12.

items.q: A class has 4 pizzas. Each student gets 18 of a pizza. How many students get a slice? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 18 pizza slices are in 4 pizzas. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 4 ÷ 18 = 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: Liam walks 15 km with his dog, 4 times a week. How far does he walk with the dog each week? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each walk is one group of 15 km. There are 4 equal groups of 15, so multiply: 4 × 15 = 45.

items.q: A trail loop at the conservation area is 12 km long. How many loops make 5 km? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 12 km loops fit in 5 km. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 5 ÷ 12 = 5 × 2 = 10.

items.q: Mei uses 13 m of ribbon for each bow. How much ribbon does she need for 8 bows? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each bow is one group of 13 m. There are 8 equal groups of 13, so multiply: 8 × 13 = 2 23.

items.q: A 2 L jug of milk is poured into cups. Each cup holds 15 L. How many cups can be filled? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 15 L cups fit in 2 L. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 2 ÷ 15 = 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: Each hockey drill at practice lasts 16 h. The coach runs 5 drills. How many hours do the drills take? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each drill is one group of 16 h. There are 5 equal groups of 16, so multiply: 5 × 16 = 56.

items.q: Owen has 9 m of rope for a canoe trip. He cuts it into pieces 12 m long. How many pieces does he get? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 12 m pieces fit in 9 m. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 9 ÷ 12 = 9 × 2 = 18.

items.q: A bag of trail mix has a mass of 110 kg. How many kilograms do 9 bags have? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Each bag is one group of 110 kg. There are 9 equal groups of 110, so multiply: 9 × 110 = 910.

items.q: A sugar shack has 6 L of maple syrup. It fills small bottles that each hold 14 L. How many bottles can it fill? Which expression answers the question?
items.e: Count how many 14 L bottles fit in 6 L. The question asks how many pieces fit, so divide: 6 ÷ 14 = 6 × 4 = 24.

items.q: Which question is answered by 3 ÷ 15?
c: How much longer is 3 m than 15 m?
A 15 m piece is cut into 3 equal parts. How long is each part?
How many 15 m pieces can you cut from 3 m of string?
How long are 3 pieces of string that are each 15 m long?
items.e: 3 ÷ 15 asks how many pieces of 15 fit in 3. That matches how many 15 m pieces are in 3 m: 3 × 5 = 15 pieces.

items.q: Which question is answered by 3 × 15?
c: How long are 3 pieces of string that are each 15 m long?
A 15 m piece is cut into 3 equal parts. How long is each part?
How much longer is 3 m than 15 m?
How many 15 m pieces can you cut from 3 m of string?
items.e: 3 × 15 means 3 groups of 15. That matches 3 pieces that are each 15 m long: 35 m in all.

items.q: Which question is answered by 4 ÷ 13?
c: How much rice is left if you use 13 cup from 4 cups?
How much rice is in each bowl if 13 cup is shared among 4 bowls?
How many 13 cup scoops of rice are in 4 cups?
How much rice is in 4 scoops that each hold 13 cup?
items.e: 4 ÷ 13 asks how many pieces of 13 fit in 4. That matches how many 13 cup scoops are in 4 cups: 4 × 3 = 12 scoops.

items.q: Which question is answered by 4 × 13?
c: How much rice is in 4 scoops that each hold 13 cup?
How much rice is left if you use 13 cup from 4 cups?
How much rice is in each bowl if 13 cup is shared among 4 bowls?
How many 13 cup scoops of rice are in 4 cups?
items.e: 4 × 13 means 4 groups of 13. That matches 4 scoops of 13 cup each: 43 = 1 13 cups.

items.q: Which question is answered by 2 ÷ 110?
c: How far do you go in 2 laps of a 110 km path?
How many laps of a 110 km path make 2 km?
What is 2 km plus 110 km?
How much farther is 2 km than 110 km?
items.e: 2 ÷ 110 asks how many pieces of 110 fit in 2. That matches how many 110 km laps make 2 km: 2 × 10 = 20 laps.

items.q: Which question is answered by 6 × 110?
c: How much farther is 6 km than 110 km?
How far do you go in 6 laps of a 110 km path?
How many laps of a 110 km path make 6 km?
What is 6 km plus 110 km?
items.e: 6 × 110 means 6 groups of 110. That matches 6 laps of 110 km: 610 km.

sets.title: Word problems: pizza, laps and more

items.q: The class orders 3 pizzas. Each pizza is cut into 8 equal slices, so each slice is 18 of a pizza. How many slices are there?
items.e: Find how many eighths are in 3 pizzas: 3 ÷ 18. Each pizza has 8 slices, so 3 pizzas have 3 × 8 = 24 slices. Check: 24 × 18 = 248 = 3.

items.q: Amira eats 3 slices of pizza. Each slice is 18 of a pizza. How much of a pizza does she eat?
c: 124 of a pizza
38 of a pizza
324 of a pizza
items.e: 3 slices of 18 each: 3 × 18. 3 × 18 means 3 groups of 18. That is 3 eighths, so the answer is 38. Do not multiply the denominator.

items.q: One lap around the school field is 14 km. Nathan runs 7 laps. How far does he run?
items.e: 7 laps of 14 km each: 7 × 14. 7 × 14 means 7 groups of 14. That is 7 fourths, so the answer is 74. 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3, so it is 1 34 km.

items.q: One lap around the school field is 14 km. Kai wants to run 3 km for the Terry Fox Run. How many laps is that?
items.e: Find how many 14 km laps fit in 3 km: 3 ÷ 14. Each kilometre is 4 laps, so 3 kilometres are 3 × 4 = 12 laps. Check: 12 × 14 = 124 = 3.

items.q: One lap of the outdoor skating rink is 110 km. Ava skates 9 laps. How far does she skate?
items.e: 9 laps of 110 km each: 9 × 110. 9 × 110 means 9 groups of 110. That is 9 tenths, so the answer is 910 km.

items.q: One lap of a skating trail is 15 km. How many laps make 2 km?
items.e: Find how many 15 km laps fit in 2 km: 2 ÷ 15. Each kilometre is 5 laps, so 2 kilometres are 2 × 5 = 10 laps. Check: 10 × 15 = 105 = 2.

items.q: A sugar shack has 5 L of maple syrup. It pours it into bottles that each hold 12 L. How many bottles can it fill?
items.e: Find how many 12 L bottles fit in 5 L: 5 ÷ 12. Each litre fills 2 bottles, so 5 litres fill 5 × 2 = 10 bottles. Check: 10 × 12 = 102 = 5.

items.q: Each batch of cookies uses 13 cup of chocolate chips. Jayden bakes 5 batches. How many cups of chocolate chips does he use?
items.e: 5 batches of 13 cup each: 5 × 13. 5 × 13 means 5 groups of 13. That is 5 thirds, so the answer is 53. 5 ÷ 3 = 1 remainder 2, so it is 1 23 cups.

items.q: At the soccer game, 4 oranges are cut into pieces. Each piece is 16 of an orange. How many pieces are there?
items.e: Find how many sixths are in 4 oranges: 4 ÷ 16. Each orange has 6 pieces, so 4 oranges have 4 × 6 = 24 pieces. Check: 24 × 16 = 246 = 4.

items.q: Lucas fills a 2 L jug using a cup that holds 14 L. How many cups does he pour in?
items.e: Find how many 14 L cups fit in 2 L: 2 ÷ 14. Each litre is 4 cups, so 2 litres are 2 × 4 = 8 cups. Check: 8 × 14 = 84 = 2.

items.q: Priya cuts 5 m of rope into pieces that are each 12 m long for knot practice. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: Find how many 12 m pieces fit in 5 m: 5 ÷ 12. Each metre makes 2 pieces, so 5 metres make 5 × 2 = 10 pieces. Check: 10 × 12 = 102 = 5.

items.q: Leah practises piano for 13 h each day. How many hours does she practise in 7 days?
items.e: 7 days of 13 h each: 7 × 13. 7 × 13 means 7 groups of 13. That is 7 thirds, so the answer is 73. 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1, so it is 2 13 h.

items.q: Each student gives a talk that lasts 16 h (10 minutes). The class has 2 h for talks. How many talks fit?
items.e: Find how many 16 h talks fit in 2 h: 2 ÷ 16. Each hour holds 6 talks, so 2 hours hold 2 × 6 = 12 talks. Check: 12 × 16 = 126 = 2.

items.q: Each tomato plant in the school garden needs 12 m of the row. The row is 9 m long. How many plants fit?
items.e: Find how many 12 m spaces fit in 9 m: 9 ÷ 12. Each metre holds 2 plants, so 9 metres hold 9 × 2 = 18 plants. Check: 18 × 12 = 182 = 9.

items.q: Arjun’s dog eats 14 kg of food each day. How much food does the dog eat in 5 days?
items.e: 5 days of 14 kg each: 5 × 14. 5 × 14 means 5 groups of 14. That is 5 fourths, so the answer is 54. 5 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 1, so it is 1 14 kg.

items.q: A bag of trail mix for the field trip has a mass of 18 kg. The class buys 9 bags. What is the total mass?
items.e: 9 bags of 18 kg each: 9 × 18. 9 × 18 means 9 groups of 18. That is 9 eighths, so the answer is 98. 9 ÷ 8 = 1 remainder 1, so it is 1 18 kg.

items.q: Each student gets 15 of a sheet of stickers. The teacher has 6 sheets. How many students get stickers?
items.e: Find how many fifths are in 6 sheets: 6 ÷ 15. Each sheet is enough for 5 students, so 6 sheets are enough for 6 × 5 = 30 students. Check: 30 × 15 = 305 = 6.

items.q: Chloe runs 5 laps of a 14 km track. Noah runs 3 laps of a 12 km track. Who runs farther?
items.e: Chloe: 5 × 14 = 54 = 1 14 km. Noah: 3 × 12 = 32 = 1 12 km. 1 12 is greater than 1 14, so Noah runs farther.

items.q: In a relay race, each of 8 runners runs 14 km. How far do the runners go altogether?
items.e: 8 runners of 14 km each: 8 × 14. 8 × 14 means 8 groups of 14. That is 8 fourths, so the answer is 84. 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so it is 2 km.

items.q: Sofia cuts 2 pizzas into slices that are each 16 of a pizza. 9 friends each eat 1 slice. How many slices are left?
items.e: First find the number of slices: 2 ÷ 16 = 2 × 6 = 12 slices. Then subtract the slices eaten: 12 − 9 = 3 slices.
